main_body: A pedestal font: a wide elliptical bowl at the top (rows ~2-8) holding blue water, on a narrow stem (rows ~9-12) with a flared base (rows ~12-14). The bowl is the largest volume.
top_band: Light grey rim ring with a blue water ellipse inside, rows ~2-6 (light grey outer rim, dark blue and light blue water inside).
evidence: The bowl reads as an ellipse seen from above. A light rim surrounds a blue water surface about 3 rows tall, much like the guide's ellipse column cap and barrel top. A front rim line closes the ellipse, and a short grey bowl belly sits below it before tapering into the stem. The stem and base are thin supports, but the main body (the bowl) shows both the opening and a front face. The bowl front face is small, which makes this borderline, but the opening is clearly visible.

style.evidence: The grey stone has about 3-4 tones (light rim, mid grey, dark grey shadow) and the water has 3 blues, so shading is reasonable but fewer steps than the Beodeul reference. The outline is a dark grey-blue that is partly tinted and partly neutral, and it is used selectively, so it is not a uniform black sticker outline. The stem and base are small, mostly flat 2-3 colour areas with little grain or speckle. The piece is small, but it is a bit thinner than the roofed well and cheese stall, which carry many more colours per tile. It is clean but a little lower in density and texture than the reference, so it fails when in doubt.
